rachel: Quick signal: after flipping the microkernel selector on canary-pool-9, host CPU p50 up ~6% and grpc smallwrite tail worsened. Anyone seen this?
omar: Saw same. Short replay (1k reqs) p50 37ms->39ms, p99 220ms->310ms. Flame points to tokenize::split and net::emit_small.
zed: The selector prefers a narrower fragment window for microkernel which increases fragment_count for many keepalive bursts. More fragments => more writev/syscalls.
probe-bot: replay summary: 1k reqs baseline p50=37ms p99=220ms; post-flip p50=39ms p99=310ms. avg writev/request +15%. kv hits steady.
rachel: Can we revert on canary and run A/B with a hybrid rule? Hybrid: microkernel only if fragments==0 and seq_len>=18.
omar: Reverting now and will run pprof snapshots + writev_count metric in replay.
probe-bot: rollback started by omar at 2026-03-24T09:02:11Z.
zed: Also prototype a kvcache-prefetch hint when chooser picks microkernel; in microbench it reduced writev ops ~7%. Keep it gated.
probe-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-24T09:05:42Z.
rachel: Good catch. Omar please run A/B and post CSV. Zed open PR for hybrid + prefetch flag. We'll validate 4h canary if A/B looks good.
zed: Will do. Closing thread until results.
